source: វិទ្យាការទប់ស្កាត់ និងកម្ចាត់សមាសភាពបទព្រុងលើដំណាំទុរេន (Prevention and Control of Harmful Organisms on Durian), Cambodian technical extension document compiled with reference to CABI Crop Protection Compendium and durian pest/disease literature, 28pp
text: Phomopsis leaf blight (Phomopsis durionis) causes blighted, browned patches on durian leaves, which can affect young flushes especially severely and, in a bad outbreak, cause significant defoliation. Damage is generally worse in humid, wet conditions and on trees already stressed by other factors. General control approach: prune out and destroy heavily affected foliage to reduce the spread of spores, improve air circulation around the canopy through appropriate spacing and pruning, and apply a fungicide during wet-season flush periods where the disease has been a recurring problem in the orchard; specific product/rate recommendations were not fully legible in the scanned source and should be confirmed locally.
